title: deliveries endpoint has no org scoping, so any user can read any endpoint's deliveries
what_is_wrong: The query filters only on WebhookDelivery.endpoint_id taken from the path and never joins WebhookEndpoint to check org_id == user.org_id, so any authenticated user can enumerate other organizations' delivery rows including response bodies.

title: user-supplied URL is fetched by the worker with no SSRF defence
what_is_wrong: The endpoint stores any host the caller supplies and the delivery worker later POSTs to it, so a customer can point an endpoint at 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 or an internal service and use the signed request as a blind SSRF probe.

title: plain http:// URLs are accepted although docs promise HTTPS only
what_is_wrong: The check `parsed.scheme.startswith("http")` passes for scheme `http`, so payloads are delivered in cleartext even though docs/webhooks.md states "Only `https://` URLs are accepted".

title: scheme validation by prefix accepts arbitrary schemes
what_is_wrong: `parsed.scheme.startswith("http")` is true for `httpfoo://host`, so an unusable scheme is persisted and only fails much later inside httpx at delivery time.

title: signing secret is readable back through the list endpoint
what_is_wrong: `WebhookEndpoint.to_dict()` includes `signing_secret` and the list route returns it for every endpoint, contradicting docs/webhooks.md ("the response is the only place the signing secret appears — it cannot be read back afterwards") and turning any read-scoped credential into secret disclosure.

title: limit query parameter has no upper bound
what_is_wrong: `Query(50, ge=1)` declares a floor but no `le`, so a caller can pass limit=10000000 and force an unbounded result set and JSON serialization of every stored payload row.

title: requested event types are never validated against the types that can fire
what_is_wrong: `event_types` is an unconstrained `list[str]`, so a typo like "invoice.payed" is accepted and the endpoint silently never receives anything.

title: endpoints can be created and listed but never deactivated or deleted
what_is_wrong: The model carries an `active` flag that only `enqueue_for_event` reads, and the diff adds no route that can set it or remove an endpoint, so a compromised or dead URL keeps receiving signed payloads.

title: unknown endpoint_id returns 200 with an empty list instead of 404
what_is_wrong: The handler never loads the endpoint, so a nonexistent id is indistinguishable from an endpoint that has no deliveries.

title: only three hardcoded event types can ever reach webhooks
what_is_wrong: `dispatch` gates the enqueue on a module-level literal set, so an endpoint registered with empty `event_types` receives just those three types and not "every event type we emit" as docs/webhooks.md promises.

title: webhook enqueue failures are swallowed, silently dropping the delivery
what_is_wrong: The `except Exception` around `enqueue_for_event` only logs a warning and returns the event id as success, so a transient DB error loses the webhook entirely with nothing to retry it, breaking the documented at-least-once guarantee.

title: event persistence and delivery enqueue are in separate transactions
what_is_wrong: The event row is committed when `session_scope` exits and `enqueue_for_event` opens its own session afterwards, so a crash between the two leaves a persisted event with no delivery rows and no mechanism that reconciles them.

title: a failing in-process subscriber prevents webhook enqueue
what_is_wrong: The `for subscriber in SUBSCRIBERS...` loop is unguarded and runs before the webhook block, so one raising subscriber aborts `dispatch` and the webhook is never enqueued.

title: the org-level webhooks_enabled flag added by the migration is never consulted
what_is_wrong: Migration 0042 adds `organizations.webhooks_enabled NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE`, but neither `dispatch` nor `enqueue_for_event` reads it, so webhooks fire for every org regardless of the flag and the flag's default suggests the opposite.

title: time.sleep() inside a coroutine blocks the whole event loop
what_is_wrong: `deliver` is async but backs off with `time.sleep(delay)`, so a single retrying delivery freezes the worker and every other delivery in the `asyncio.gather` batch for up to 16 seconds at a time.

title: ORM rows are used after their session closes, so attribute access raises DetachedInstanceError
what_is_wrong: `_claim_batch` returns `WebhookDelivery` instances after `session_scope` exits and commits, and `deliver`/`send_once` then read `delivery.payload`, `delivery.attempts` and `delivery.id` on expired, detached objects.

title: endpoint is loaded then used outside its session
what_is_wrong: `endpoint = session.get(m.WebhookEndpoint, ...)` is fetched inside `with session_scope()` but `endpoint.signing_secret` and `endpoint.url` are read in `send_once` after the session closed, so the attribute load fails on a detached instance.

title: a deleted endpoint yields AttributeError on None
what_is_wrong: `session.get` returns None when the endpoint row is gone (cascade delete), and the code passes it straight to `send_once` without a None check.

title: the signature is computed over different bytes than the request body
what_is_wrong: `sign` hashes `json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)` while the request is sent with `client.post(..., json=delivery.payload)`, which serializes with httpx's own key order and separators, so the HMAC never matches the raw body a receiver verifies.

title: the timestamp header is not covered by the signature
what_is_wrong: `sign` returns a timestamp but MACs only the payload, so `X-Acme-Timestamp` is unauthenticated and an attacker can rewrite it freely, defeating the five-minute replay window docs/webhooks.md tells customers to rely on.

title: full request headers including the signature are logged at INFO
what_is_wrong: `log.info("POST %s headers=%s", endpoint.url, headers)` writes the computed `X-Acme-Signature` and timestamp into application logs, so anyone with log access can replay a valid signed request.

title: 4xx responses are retried although the docs call them permanent
what_is_wrong: The success branch checks only `200 <= status < 300` and everything else falls through to the retry path, so a 400 or 404 is hammered five times, contradicting "a 4xx is permanent and we stop immediately".

title: the status written on permanent failure violates the migration's CHECK constraint
what_is_wrong: `_finish(..., "failed_permanent", ...)` stores a value the `webhook_deliveries` CHECK allows only as `'failed'`, so every permanently failed delivery aborts its transaction with a constraint violation.

title: get-then-set lock acquisition is not atomic
what_is_wrong: Two workers can both see an empty `LOCK_KEY` before either writes it, so both proceed to claim and deliver the same batch; the check needs a single SET NX.

title: SET and EXPIRE are separate calls, so a crash leaves a lock with no TTL
what_is_wrong: If the process dies between `redis_client.set` and `redis_client.expire`, `LOCK_KEY` persists forever and every worker afterwards spins on the poll interval without ever dispatching.

title: the lock is deleted without checking ownership
what_is_wrong: `redis_client.delete(LOCK_KEY)` in the `finally` removes whatever value is there, so a worker that overran the 60s TTL deletes the lock a second worker legitimately acquired.

title: batch processing can far outlive the 60-second lock TTL
what_is_wrong: The lock expires after 60s while `asyncio.gather` may run five attempts with 30s timeouts and blocking backoffs, so another worker acquires the lock and re-processes rows the first worker still holds.

title: `batch` is referenced outside the try, so a claim failure raises UnboundLocalError
what_is_wrong: If `_claim_batch()` raises, the `finally` releases the lock and control reaches `if not batch:` with `batch` never assigned, crashing the worker loop with a NameError instead of the original error.

title: rows marked in_flight are never recovered after a worker dies
what_is_wrong: `_claim_batch` flips status to "in_flight" and commits, and nothing resets stale in_flight rows or catches exceptions from `gather`, so a crash or unhandled error strands those deliveries permanently outside the pending query.

title: asyncio.gather without return_exceptions aborts the whole batch
what_is_wrong: One delivery raising a non-`httpx.HTTPError` exception (for example `httpx.InvalidURL` or `UnsupportedProtocol` from a stored bogus scheme) propagates out of `gather` and out of `run_worker`, killing the worker and leaving sibling deliveries unfinished.

title: claiming relies solely on the Redis lock with no row-level locking
what_is_wrong: The SELECT has no `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and the status flip happens in a read-then-write gap, so any concurrent claimer (or a lock failure) produces duplicate deliveries.

title: naive datetime.utcnow() is written to a timezone-aware column and compared to an aware now()
what_is_wrong: `next_attempt_at=datetime.utcnow()` produces a naive value while `_claim_batch` filters with `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`, so the comparison depends on the driver's interpretation and misfires by the server's UTC offset.

title: attempts and next_attempt_at are only persisted at terminal state
what_is_wrong: The retry ladder runs entirely in memory and `_finish` writes once at the end, so `attempts` stays 0 and `next_attempt_at` never advances during retries, making the deliveries API's "when the next attempt is scheduled" wrong and losing all progress if the worker restarts.

title: backoff has no jitter despite the documented "exponential with jitter"
what_is_wrong: `timedelta(seconds=BASE_DELAY_SECONDS**attempt)` is fully deterministic, so all endpoints failing together retry in lockstep thundering herds.

title: the row fetched for finishing is used without a None check
what_is_wrong: `session.get(m.WebhookDelivery, delivery_id)` can return None if the row was deleted by endpoint cascade, and the next line assigns `row.status` on None.

title: the entire response body is stored unbounded in the database
what_is_wrong: `response_body = detail` persists `response.text` from an arbitrary customer server, so a multi-megabyte or attacker-controlled body is written verbatim into `webhook_deliveries` and later served back through the deliveries API.

title: follow_redirects=True lets a customer redirect a signed request to another host
what_is_wrong: The shared `httpx.AsyncClient` follows redirects, so a registered HTTPS endpoint can 302 the signed payload to an internal address or a third party, bypassing whatever validation was done on the stored URL.

title: no bound on delivery concurrency
what_is_wrong: `asyncio.gather` fans out all `BATCH_SIZE` = 100 deliveries at once with no semaphore, so one batch can open 100 simultaneous outbound connections.

title: synchronous DB work runs inside coroutines
what_is_wrong: `enqueue_for_event`, `_claim_batch` and `_finish` do blocking SQLAlchemy calls with no await, so every DB round trip stalls the event loop the worker shares with in-flight HTTP requests.

title: the delivered body carries no event id, so receivers cannot deduplicate
what_is_wrong: The request body is the bare internal event payload with no envelope, yet docs/webhooks.md instructs customers to "deduplicate on `event_id`" — a field that is never transmitted in the body or headers.

title: one endpoint row is re-fetched per delivery
what_is_wrong: Each `deliver` call opens its own `session_scope` and loads the endpoint, so a batch of 100 deliveries for one endpoint issues 100 identical queries.

title: signing secrets come from the non-cryptographic `random` module
what_is_wrong: `random.choice` draws from a seeded Mersenne Twister, so observing a few secrets lets an attacker reconstruct the generator state and forge signatures for other tenants; `secrets` is required here.

title: signature comparison is not constant time
what_is_wrong: `return expected == signature` uses ordinary string equality, leaking timing information about the correct digest, while the docs tell customers to use a constant-time comparison the library itself does not.

title: verify recomputes a fresh timestamp and ignores the one it was given
what_is_wrong: `verify` calls `sign` again, discarding the returned timestamp and never accepting or checking the received `X-Acme-Timestamp`, so it cannot enforce the documented five-minute replay window at all.

title: SECRET_BYTES counts alphabet characters, not bytes
what_is_wrong: The constant is used as `range(SECRET_BYTES)` over a 62-character alphabet, so it names a character count and misstates the entropy of the secret it produces.

title: the canonical form is not the bytes the receiver sees
what_is_wrong: `json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True)` uses Python's default separators and non-ASCII escaping and is documented nowhere, so even a receiver told to re-serialize cannot reproduce it.

title: to_dict unconditionally exposes the signing secret
what_is_wrong: Every caller of `to_dict()` — including the list route — gets `signing_secret`, so the model itself makes secret leakage the default rather than the create-response-only behaviour the docs describe.

title: the model declares timezone-aware columns that the migration creates as TIMESTAMP without time zone
what_is_wrong: `created_at`, `updated_at` and `next_attempt_at` are `DateTime(timezone=True)` in SQLAlchemy but `TIMESTAMP` in migration 0042, so offsets are discarded on write and values come back naive.

title: the STATUSES tuple is dead and disagrees with the DB constraint
what_is_wrong: `STATUSES` is defined but referenced nowhere, and it lists `failed_permanent` while the migration's CHECK lists `failed`, so it documents a state machine neither the code nor the schema enforces.

title: updated_at has no onupdate, so most writes leave it stale
what_is_wrong: Only `_finish` sets `updated_at` explicitly; `_claim_batch`'s status flip to in_flight does not, so the column does not track the last modification.

title: column type disagrees with the migration
what_is_wrong: The model declares `String(100)` while the migration creates `event_type TEXT`, so model-level assumptions about length are not backed by the schema.

title: the unique index on event_id alone allows only one endpoint per event
what_is_wrong: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON webhook_deliveries (event_id)` makes the second row inserted by `enqueue_for_event` for an org with two endpoints violate uniqueness, so the whole enqueue fails and every extra endpoint gets nothing.

title: the CHECK allows 'failed' but the code only ever writes 'failed_permanent'
what_is_wrong: The constraint list `('pending', 'in_flight', 'delivered', 'failed')` does not contain the literal `_finish` uses for exhausted retries, so permanent failures can never be recorded.

title: the claim query's index is missing its sort column
what_is_wrong: The only index is on `(status)` while `_claim_batch` filters status plus `next_attempt_at <= now` and orders by `next_attempt_at`, so the scheduler sorts a large status='pending' partition on every poll.

title: no index on endpoint_id for the deliveries listing and FK cascade
what_is_wrong: `list_deliveries` filters `endpoint_id` and orders by `created_at` with no supporting index, and the `ON DELETE CASCADE` FK also needs one to avoid a full scan per endpoint deletion.

title: no index on org_id
what_is_wrong: Both `list_webhook_endpoints` and `enqueue_for_event` filter `org_id`, and the table is created without an index on it.

title: nothing prevents duplicate endpoints for the same org and URL
what_is_wrong: There is no unique constraint on `(org_id, url)`, so a client that posts the registration twice gets two endpoints and every event is delivered twice with different secrets.

title: the DB has no default for status while the model does
what_is_wrong: `status TEXT NOT NULL` without `DEFAULT 'pending'` means any insert path that bypasses the SQLAlchemy default fails, splitting the source of truth for the initial state.

title: shared secrets are stored in plaintext
what_is_wrong: `signing_secret TEXT NOT NULL` keeps every tenant's HMAC key readable to anyone with database or backup access, with no encryption or key-management indirection.

title: the ALTER shares a transaction with the table creation
what_is_wrong: Adding a NOT NULL column to `organizations` takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock held for the duration of the whole migration transaction, coupling an unrelated hot table to the new-table DDL.

title: the migration has no rollback path
what_is_wrong: Only forward DDL is provided, so the two new tables and the `organizations.webhooks_enabled` column cannot be reverted if the release is rolled back.

title: deliveries store a full payload copy with no retention or pruning
what_is_wrong: Every event is duplicated as JSONB per endpoint alongside the response body, and nothing in the migration or code deletes old rows, so the table grows without bound and retains customer payloads indefinitely.

title: the test captures the body and the signature but never checks one against the other
what_is_wrong: It asserts only that the signature header starts with "sha256=", so the mismatch between `serialize()` and httpx's own JSON encoding passes green and the test reads as coverage of signing while proving nothing about it.

title: the retry, finish, claim, lock and worker logic added by the diff is untested
what_is_wrong: Only `sign`/`verify`/`backoff_for`/`send_once` are exercised; `deliver`, `_finish`, `_claim_batch`, `_acquire_lock` and `run_worker` — where the blocking sleep, status-constraint mismatch and lock races live — have no tests at all.

title: the round-trip test is tautological
what_is_wrong: `verify` calls `sign` internally with the same secret and ignores timestamps, so the assertion holds by construction and cannot fail for any property a real receiver checks.

title: the secret test pins format only, not unpredictability
what_is_wrong: It asserts prefix and character count, so a generator returning a constant string of the right shape would pass, which is exactly the class of defect `random.choice` represents.

title: hand-rolled fakes of the ORM models hide the detached-instance failure
what_is_wrong: `send_once` is only ever called with plain classes whose attributes are always available, so the tests cannot surface that real `WebhookEndpoint`/`WebhookDelivery` objects are expired and detached by the time they are read.

title: the backoff parametrisation skips the boundary attempts
what_is_wrong: Only attempts 1 through 4 are checked, so `backoff_for(0)` returning 1s and the behaviour at MAX_ATTEMPTS are unspecified by any test.

title: nothing tests the endpoint-registration URL validation
what_is_wrong: The new `create_webhook_endpoint` scheme check has no test, so its acceptance of `http://` and of arbitrary `http`-prefixed schemes is unguarded against regression.
